analyst_view.overall: Early view: Brighton are second after a 1-0 win at Manchester City and a 2-0 home win over Brentford, and they are also in the Champions League this season. Hull are 13th with three draws in their last five and a long injury list, including Eliot Matazo, Matt Targett, Charlie Hughes and Hidemasa Morita. Hull held Arsenal goalless until the 72nd minute, and a similar deep plan is likely here.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. I lean slightly lower: Hull kept Arsenal out until the 72nd minute and have drawn three of their last five, and Brighton's two latest league wins both came with clean sheets. A 1-0 or 1-1 kind of game looks likely.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, 5.2 of them for Brighton. I lean slightly higher: if Hull sit deep again, Brighton will spend long spells around the box and win corners from blocked crosses and shots.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards. I lean higher: Hull had six names in the book at the Emirates, and Brighton were booked four times against ten-man Brentford. A side defending deep for 90 minutes against quick passing tends to pick up yellows.

shots.text: The numbers say 27 shots, 17 of them Brighton's. That looks fair: Brighton will dominate the ball while Hull's own attempts will be few, so I stay close to the site.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: a packed Hull defence blocks plenty, Hull's own threat is limited with Ilyas Ansah injured, and Brighton are without Kaoru Mitoma and Evan Ferguson.
